1. Executive Summary
The JGH Intelligence Engine (Agentic Analyst) is a production-grade, enterprise AI-powered Text-to-SQL Business
Intelligence platform built for JGH's internal operations team. It enables non-technical business users — managers,
analysts, and operations staff — to query a live enterprise MySQL database using plain English, receive verified SQL
results in real time, and export reports in PDF, Excel, or CSV format — all without writing a single line of SQL.
The system was built from scratch over approximately 6 weeks of iterative development, evolving from a simple
prototype into a robust, multi-stage, self-correcting agentic pipeline that enforces strict read-only access, detects
hallucinations, validates SQL using Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) parsing, and guarantees that every response is traceable
to an exact database row.

2. Project Goal and Motivation
2.1 The Problem
JGH's operations team regularly needs answers to business questions such as: who are the top retailers by earnings this
month, how do June and July transaction volumes compare, or which mechanics in Bengaluru have KYC verified status.
Before this system, answering these required a data analyst to manually write MySQL queries, export to Excel, and share
results — a process taking 1–3 days per request, dependent on a bottlenecked resource, and inaccessible to
non-technical users.
2.2 The Goal
1. Understand natural language business questions in plain English
2. Translate questions into accurate, safe MySQL SELECT queries using a local or cloud LLM
3. Validate generated SQL against the live database schema (no hallucinated column names)
4. Execute SQL on the live database and capture exact results in a verified model
5. Generate a grounded natural language response strictly based on returned database rows
6. Present results in a rich web dashboard with tables, charts, SQL viewer, and export buttons
7. Enforce strict security — read-only access, no credentials exposed, no destructive operations
2.3 Design Philosophy — Single Source of Truth
"Every answer shown to the user must be provably grounded in an exact database row. No invented numbers.
No hallucinated values. The UI, the exports, and the natural language answer must all read from the same
canonical VerifiedResult object."

10.1 SQL Extraction (5-Step Parsing)
The LLM output is NEVER trusted raw. A 5-step extraction pipeline handles all observed model output formats:
Step
Handles
Example Input
1
Strip <think>...</think> blocks
DeepSeek / Qwen CoT reasoning chains
2
Extract from ```sql code blocks
Model-wrapped markdown fences
3
Detect Write:/Query:/SQL: markers
Prefixed output formats
4
Find first SELECT or WITH line
Natural language followed by SQL
5
Semicolon truncation
Prevent multi-statement injection
10.2 Self-Correction Loop (Max 3 Attempts)
When SQL generation fails validation, the error message is explicitly injected into the next generation prompt. The LLM
receives its own mistake description and corrects it.

If Failed

Generate SQL from grounded prompt
Inject error: 'Column total_amount does not exist'
2
Regenerate with error feedback
Inject error: 'Table alias wt used without definition'
3

Return ERROR status to user

Before ANY pipeline processing, the user's question is checked against a security word list. If matched, the request is

19. Challenges and Solutions
19.1 SQL Hallucination of Column Names
Problem
The 
LLM 
frequently 
invented 
column 
names 
(wallet_transaction.total_amount,
users.retailer_name). Root cause: LLM trained on generic SQL patterns hallucinated
plausible-sounding names.
Solution
Three-layer system: (1) AST alias resolver maps SQL aliases to actual tables, (2)
Schema Column Validator checks every column against schema_metadata.json, (3)
Self-correction loop feeds error messages into retry prompt.
Result
Column hallucination errors reduced from ~40% to <5%.
19.2 Ambiguous Business Terminology
Problem
Users say 'retailers', 'earnings', 'box scans' — the LLM doesn't know these map to specific
SQL columns and WHERE filters.
Solution
Business Dictionary encodes: 'retailer' → users WHERE user_role=2, 'earnings' →
wallet_transaction.amount, 'box scans' → COUNT(sku_inventories.id).
Result
100% of core business queries handled correctly.
19.3 Remote Database Connectivity Failures
Problem
Production MySQL at 168.144.28.208:3306 is sometimes offline, causing 30-second TCP
timeout delays for every query.
Solution
Circuit Breaker pattern: first failure instantly opens circuit, all subsequent requests route
to SQLite (0ms overhead), 150ms TCP probe every 600 seconds checks recovery.
Result
Timeout delay eliminated from 30,000ms to 0ms.
19.4 LLM Response Format Unpredictability
Problem
Models return SQL in different formats: markdown fences, thinking blocks, natural
language prefix, or SQL buried in explanatory text.
Solution
5-step extraction pipeline: strip blocks, extract ```sql fences, detect Write:/Query: markers,
find first SELECT/WITH line, semicolon truncation.
Result
100% extraction success rate across all tested model outputs.
19.5 LLM Date Hallucination
Problem
LLM invented wrong date boundaries using CURRENT_DATE(), NOW(), or hardcoded
wrong dates.
Solution
Pre-compute all dates in resolve_runtime_dates() and inject exact strings '2026-07-01
00:00:00' directly into prompt. LLM only writes WHERE clause structure.
Result
Zero date-related failures after implementation.

23. Conclusion
The JGH Intelligence Engine represents a complete end-to-end implementation of a production-grade enterprise AI
Text-to-SQL system built over 6 weeks of iterative development.
23.1 Key Technical Achievements
Multi-Stage Agentic Pipeline: 7-stage pipeline with NLP understanding, knowledge-grounded prompt engineering,
LLM SQL generation, AST validation, database execution, and verified response generation.
Zero-Hallucination Answer Layer: 100% answer accuracy across all benchmark cases. The integrity verification
system guarantees no fabricated values reach the user.
Production-Grade Security: Six-layer defense-in-depth architecture blocking SQL injection, credential access, DDL
operations, and hallucinated column access.
Resilient Database Layer: Circuit breaker pattern enabling seamless MySQL → SQLite fallback with 0ms overhead
when remote is unavailable.
Multi-Model LLM Architecture: Provider-agnostic design supporting Gemini, Groq, and local Ollama with per-stage
routing and automatic fallback.
Self-Correcting SQL Loop: 3-attempt self-correction with explicit error feedback enabling the LLM to fix its own
column and table mistakes.
